name: WA-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Adam Smith's long tenure and large financial edge
Prediction markets price Smith near-certain to win
model.rationale: Adam Smith holds a heavily Democratic seat with a two-decade incumbency advantage and roughly $1.9 million raised against a challenger who has raised about $12,000, with no outside spending on either side. Markets price Smith at about 97% to win, and fundamentals point to a margin in the mid-20s.
model.watch: A surprise would require an unforeseen scandal or external shock, since the challenger lacks the resources to compete.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Adam Smith, a longtime Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a Seattle-area district that leans Democratic by more than 20 points. He has raised nearly $1.9 million and holds about $870,000 on hand, while Republican Doug Basler has raised only about $12,000 with no outside spending in the race. No general-election polls or expert ratings are available, but prediction markets give Smith roughly a 97% chance of winning.

The combination of district lean, incumbency, and an overwhelming financial gap makes this one of the safest Democratic holds on the ballot. An expected margin in the mid-20s carries meaningful uncertainty only because no polling exists, but the fundamentals leave little room for an upset.
